expected.note: Survival is token survival, not accuracy, and it is measured against a script rather than a transcript. These ranges exist to catch a regression in the pipeline, not to certify a benchmark. No requirement is declared must_keep, because nothing in this corpus survived at every setting and claiming otherwise would be a promise the evidence does not support.

limitations: Six captures and sixteen runs, one speaker, one session per day. That is enough to show an effect is real and to characterise its spread. No confidence interval is claimed, and the settings are not evenly sampled: two captures are missing one setting each, so n differs by row.

The utterances are technical instructions the author wrote and then read aloud, deliberately dense with filenames, numerals and prohibitions. They are not a random sample of development speech and the effects here are upper bounds on how often they occur.
The spoken side is the script, not a transcript. A local ASR engine read the same audio and disagreed with Wispr in both directions, so neither is treated as ground truth.

Number folding treats a bare unit word that is also a number word as a number, so 'one file' becomes '1 file'. Both sides fold identically so nothing is lost, but the token count is not the raw count of what was said.
A number run broken by a non-number word is left alone, so 'two point none' stays as written. That protects version strings at the cost of missing a decimal that was genuinely spelled out.

Backslash escaping is undone outside code spans as well as inside them, because escaped backticks make a code span impossible to detect reliably. A backslash that a reader would actually see is therefore scored as surviving.
Reading pace was not held constant across the passes.
Audio is not published, because it contains a voice.
findings: Cleanup is not reliably worse, it is wildly variable. Across these captures raw passthrough spans 4.8 points, Light 34.9 and Medium 41.0. On u4 both rewrite settings scored a clean 100% while raw passthrough scored 97.6%, and on u5 all three tied at 100%.
On u1, at both rewrite settings, 'no pytest' arrived as 'not pytest'. That is the opposite instruction, delivered without any error. Raw passthrough delivered it correctly.

On u1 the only requirement either rewrite setting lost was the version constraint 3.10; the filenames and the 0.7 threshold both arrived intact, because what had looked like filename damage was markdown escaping. On u4 the rewrite settings lost nothing at all. The same setting produced both.
Spelled-out numbers and markdown-escaped identifiers were initially scored as losses. Both were scorer faults rather than pipeline damage, and fixing them moved every figure in this corpus.

The capture marker was itself subject to dictation corruption: across sixteen runs it arrived intact in six, as 'and utterance' in four and as a bare 'utterance' in three, and the remainder carried a trailing conjunction. Those remnants were stripped from the stored text before measurement, because scaffolding that survives into a measurement is scaffolding the tool has to know about.

A unit abbreviation is not a loss: '240 pixels' arriving as 240px still says 240, and '8 pixels' arriving as 8px still says 8. The mirror case, '1rem' becoming 'one rem', is a real loss, because a literal became prose.
